title: A larger settling bead
hook: Change sphere radius and predict terminal speed.
misconception: terminal speed doubles when sphere radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v_t = 2Δρgr²/(9η) to compare terminal speed when sphere radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a small sphere denser than the fluid in Stokes flow with fixed fluid viscosity and density difference, v_t = 2Δρgr²/(9η). When sphere radius doubles, terminal speed becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v_t = 2Δρgr²/(9η); scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a small sphere denser than the fluid in Stokes flow with fixed fluid viscosity and density difference, with a nonzero initial result. If sphere radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on terminal speed?
recall.why: Apply v_t = 2Δρgr²/(9η) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
